about.title: Downey Workplace Injury Claims
about.longDescription: Downey sits in the middle of Los Angeles County, and much of its workday happens in motion: deliveries running along Firestone Boulevard, crews heading to job sites off Lakewood Boulevard, service vans moving between Florence Avenue and Paramount Boulevard. When someone gets hurt doing that work, two systems may apply at once. Workers' compensation covers medical care and part of lost wages no matter who was at fault, and it is normally the only claim you can bring against your own employer. A separate injury claim can still exist against a negligent third party, such as a subcontractor on a shared site, a property owner who ignored a hazard, the maker of a faulty tool, or another driver. That last one matters here. Downey recorded 829 injury collisions in 2025, with 1,234 people hurt, and reports tend to cluster on Fridays between 3 and 5 p.m., right as many shifts wind down. Our team reviews both your workers' compensation eligibility and any potential third-party claims to ensure you understand which paths apply to your situation.

items.title: Both claims, not just one
items.desc: Workers' compensation is usually your only remedy against your employer, but a negligent subcontractor, property owner, equipment maker, or driver can be held separately responsible. We can evaluate whether a third-party claim exists alongside your comp case.

items.title: Deadlines handled early
items.desc: California asks you to report a work injury to your employer within 30 days, and third-party injury claims carry a two-year filing window. Acting quickly helps keep both clocks in view.

items.title: Protection if your employer pushes back
items.desc: Retaliating against a worker for reporting an injury or filing a comp claim is illegal in California. We can step in if your hours are cut, your role changes, or you're let go after speaking up.

items.question: I was rear-ended on Lakewood Boulevard while driving a company vehicle. Is that a workers' comp case or a car accident case?
items.answer: It can be both. Because you were working, workers' compensation should cover your medical treatment and part of your lost wages regardless of fault. Since another driver caused the crash, you may also have a separate injury claim against that driver, and that claim can cover losses comp does not, such as pain and suffering. We can coordinate the two so one does not undercut the other.

items.question: Do I really have to report the injury to my employer within 30 days?
items.answer: Yes, California expects notice to your employer within 30 days of the injury, and waiting can complicate your comp benefits. Report it in writing if you can, even if the injury seems minor at first. If more than 30 days have passed, don't assume you're out of options; contact us to discuss where you stand.

items.question: Can I be fired for filing a workers' comp claim in Downey?
items.answer: No. California law makes it illegal for an employer to retaliate against you for reporting a workplace injury or pursuing compensation. If you notice a demotion, sudden schedule cuts, or termination after your report, document the timeline and reach out to us. Retaliation can become its own claim.
